newsitem.title: USA: U.S. thrifts post $505 mln Q3 loss - OTS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. thrifts post $505 mln Q3 loss - OTS.

text.p: The nation's thrift industry posted a $505 million loss in the third quarter because of a one-time special assessment by the government to replenish the fund that protects depositors at failed savings and loans institutions, regulators said Wednesday.
The Office of Thrift Supervision added, however, that the industry should return "to its stable profitability" in the fourth quarter.
The special assessment to fully capitalize the Savings Association Insurance Fund (SAIF) cost OTS-regulated thrifts $3.2 billion before taxes, or an estimated $2.1 billion after taxes.
Without the expense, S&L's would have earned an estimated $1.6 billion, the same as a year earlier but down from a record $1.9 billion in the second quarter.
"I believe it is a clear indication of the underlying strength of the thrift industry that it was able to absorb the one-time assessment in a single quarter," said OTS Director Nicholas Retsinas.
"The important fact is that the one-time charge is now behind us, and with the SAIF fully capitalized, the insurance premium for thrifts is more in line with what banks pay."
The special assessment stemmed from legislation enacted this year which imposed a one-time increase in the premiums thrifts pay for deposit insurance.

The assessment resulted in return on average assets (ROA) of minus 26 basis points. Without the special assessment, the ROA would have been 82 basis points, the same as a year ago but down from 101 basis points in the second quarter.
The percentage of thrifts that met or exceeded "well-capitalized" standards was 95 percent, down slightly from 97 percent in the prior three quarters.
The number of OTS-regulated thrifts fell to 1,378 from 1,397 in the second quarter.
The OTS counted 31 "problem" thrifts in the third quarter, down from 33 in the previous quarter. Troubled assets totaled $9.3 billion, unchanged from the second quarter.
